findings.claim: The game clock keeps running while the app's own modal "Ready to finish" alert blocks all input, and that dead time lands in the result the win overlay reports (and in the stored best time): with the alert up and no input possible the header clock advanced 3:42 -> 4:28 over a 45 s wall-clock window.

repro: inject the pinned fixture save (.qa-loop/evidence/round-1/wf-4-1/save69.json, deal #10011 at move 69) with .qa-loop/evidence/round-1/wf-4-1/inject.sh
tap the 9-of-spades run head at (224,590) -> board becomes finishable, 'Ready to finish' alert appears
do nothing for 45 s; read the header Time behind the alert

findings.note: TRAP: the naive fix (pause GameClock while a modal is up) turns any sheet — Daily, Wins, How to play — into a pause button and corrupts recorded best times. If anything is done here, scope it to the app-initiated auto-finish alert only (e.g. subtract the alert's dwell), and leave user-opened sheets alone.

findings.claim: 'Not yet' stops the auto-finish prompt only for the life of the process: the app re-offers 'Ready to finish' the moment the very same game is restored after an app kill/cold relaunch (same deal, same move count, same clock), so the promise that it will not nag again this game is broken by any process restart.

repro: inject save69.json (deal #10011, move 69) and launch with Auto-finish: Ask
tap 'Not yet' (128,497) -> alert gone, gold Finish pill present, Moves 70
xcrun simctl terminate <udid> com.whimsicaldistractions.Causeway; xcrun simctl launch ... (same game restores: Deal #10011, Moves 70)
the 'Ready to finish' alert is on screen again

findings.note: autoFinishDeferred is not part of Game.SavedGame and restore() resets it to false before calling maybeAutoFinish(). Fix is an optional field on the persisted save — decode defensively so old saves still load (fix_risk: state-migration).

findings.claim: After a win, tapping Close and then Undo un-wins the completed deal: the last card comes back out of the foundation, the game clock resumes on a deal that is already banked, the Finish pill reappears, and tapping it fires a second 'You solved it!' overlay for the same deal with a worse time (98 moves 3:07 -> 98 moves 3:45). The loop can be repeated indefinitely.

repro: inject save95.json (deal #10011, move 95, 3 cards left) with inject.sh; prefs causeway.autoplay=false, causeway.autofinishmode=off
launch; tap (126,500), (126,470), (77,470) to send the last three cards home -> win overlay 'Deal #10,011 - 98 moves - 3:07'
tap Close (314,488) -> solved board, Undo is ENABLED
tap Undo (142,135) -> Moves 97, 8-of-diamonds is back in the tableau, clock running again, Finish pill back
tap Finish (167,175) -> a second 'You solved it!' overlay, 'Deal #10,011 - 98 moves - 3:45'

findings.note: No data corruption observed: WinStore keeps min(moves,secs) per deal and the Won counter (distinct deals) stays 1, so the repeat overlays cannot improve or damage a record. TRAP: disabling Undo once a deal is complete is a behaviour change and also touches the daily-attempt path (an undo after a recorded daily win bumps telem.undos) — human call, and worth checking DailyStore before changing anything.
